confusables.difference: Poor quality means badly made. Cheap means low in price. Something cheap can still be good, and something expensive can be poor quality.

entry_json.definition: modern popular music with a strong beat, liked by many young people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I grew up listening to pop, but now I prefer quieter music.
example_sentences: Pop music from the eighties is popular again.
She sings in a pop band at weekends.

entry_json.definition: liked or enjoyed by many people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Cycling has become very popular in my city since the new lanes were built.
example_sentences: That beach is popular with families in the summer.
The most popular subject at the college is business.
entry_json.avoid: Use popular with people, not popular by: popular with students.

entry_json.definition: all the people who live in a place, or the number of them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The population of my home town has doubled in twenty years.
example_sentences: An ageing population puts pressure on health services.
The city has a population of about two million.

confusables.difference: Population is the whole group counted as one thing and takes a singular verb: the population is growing. People is plural: people are moving to the cities.

entry_json.definition: the place where someone or something is, or a job in a company
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She applied for a position in the research department.
example_sentences: Move the chair into a comfortable position.
The company is in a strong financial position.

entry_json.definition: good or useful, or feeling hopeful about the future
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Living abroad had a positive effect on my confidence.
example_sentences: The response from customers has been very positive.
Try to stay positive during a long job search.

confusables.difference: They are opposites. A positive effect helps and a negative effect harms. Task 2 questions often ask whether a change is positive or negative.

entry_json.definition: something that you own, or the state of having something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: When I moved abroad, I took only the possessions that fitted in two cases.
example_sentences: The most valuable possession in the house was an old clock.
Personal possessions are not covered by the insurance.

entry_json.definition: something that might happen or might be true
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a real possibility that sea levels will rise faster than expected.
example_sentences: We should consider the possibility of working from home.
The possibility of failure did not stop her applying.

confusables.difference: A possibility is only something that might happen. An opportunity is a good chance you can take. Say I had the opportunity to study abroad, not the possibility.

entry_json.avoid: Use the possibility of doing something, not the possibility to do something.

entry_json.definition: able to happen or be done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It is possible to reach the airport by train in under an hour.
example_sentences: Please reply as soon as possible.
Is it possible to change the date of the test?
entry_json.avoid: Say it is possible to do something or it is possible that something will happen. Do not say I am possible to come.

entry_json.definition: the system of sending letters and parcels, or the letters that arrive
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sent the documents by post because they had to be signed.
example_sentences: The post arrives before nine every weekday.
Her results came in the post two weeks later.

confusables.difference: Post is the usual British word for letters and the service that carries them. Mail is the American word, and is also used everywhere for email.

entry_json.definition: a large printed sheet with a picture or information, put up on a wall
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There were posters advertising the concert all over the campus.
example_sentences: The students made a poster about recycling.
A poster in the waiting room explained the new opening hours.

entry_json.definition: a round white vegetable with a brown skin that grows under the ground
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Potatoes are cheap and store well, so I always keep some at home.
example_sentences: Boil the potatoes for about twenty minutes.
Potatoes are the main crop in that region.
entry_json.avoid: The plural adds es: potatoes, not potatos.

entry_json.definition: the unit of money used in Britain
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A monthly travel card costs about ninety pounds in this city.
example_sentences: The book cost twelve pounds fifty.
The pound fell against the dollar last week.
entry_json.avoid: After a number, keep pound singular in compound adjectives: a ten pound note, but the ticket costs ten pounds.

entry_json.definition: the ability to control people or events, or energy used to make machines work
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Local councils have little power over how the money is spent.
example_sentences: The storm cut off power to thousands of homes.
Wind power now supplies a large share of our electricity.

confusables.difference: In everyday and technical use they overlap, but power is the rate at which energy is used, and it also means control over others. Energy never means control.

entry_json.definition: doing something many times so that you get better at it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Regular practice matters far more than long sessions once a week.
example_sentences: Speaking practice is the fastest way to improve fluency.
In practice, the new rule changed very little.

confusables.difference: In British English, practice with a c is the noun and practise with an s is the verb: I need more practice, so I practise every day. American English spells both practice.

entry_json.definition: to do something many times so that you become better at it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I practise speaking English with a friend for twenty minutes every evening.
example_sentences: She practises the piano before school.
Practise writing under time pressure before the real test.

confusables.difference: Practise with an s is the verb; practice with a c is the noun. A tip that works: advise and advice follow the same pattern, and you can hear the difference there.

entry_json.avoid: After practise, use the ing form: practise writing, not practise to write.

entry_json.definition: to say what you think will happen in the future
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Economists predict that housing costs will keep rising.
example_sentences: It is hard to predict how the technology will develop.
Nobody predicted such a sharp fall in numbers.

entry_json.definition: to like one thing more than another
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I prefer studying in the morning because my mind is clearer.
example_sentences: Most students prefer online lectures to early morning classes.
I would prefer to sit near the window.
entry_json.avoid: Use to, not than, after prefer: I prefer tea to coffee. With would prefer, use to plus a verb: I would prefer to walk.

entry_json.definition: to get something or yourself ready for something that will happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I spent two months preparing for the test after work.
example_sentences: She prepared a short presentation for the meeting.
Prepare a list of questions before the interview.
entry_json.avoid: Use prepare for something, but prepare to do something: prepare for the test, prepare to leave.

entry_json.definition: a thing that you give to someone, usually on a special day
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I bought my sister a book as a present for finishing her degree.
example_sentences: Children receive presents on their birthdays.
She wrapped the present in brown paper.

confusables.difference: They mean the same thing. Present is the everyday spoken word; gift sounds slightly more formal and appears in shops and writing.

entry_json.avoid: The stress changes with the meaning: a PREsent that you give, but to preSENT the results.

entry_json.definition: the leader of a country that has no king or queen, or the head of an organization
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The president is elected every four years in that country.
example_sentences: She was elected president of the students union.
The president gave a short speech at the opening.

entry_json.definition: quite, but not extremely; also, as an adjective, attractive to look at
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The exam was pretty difficult, but I finished every section.
example_sentences: I am pretty sure the library closes at eight.
It was a pretty village with a river running through it.
entry_json.avoid: Pretty meaning quite is informal. In Task 2 writing use fairly, quite or rather instead.

entry_json.definition: to stop something from happening
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Better street lighting can prevent accidents at night.
example_sentences: Regular exercise helps prevent heart disease.
Nothing prevented her from applying a second time.

confusables.difference: Prevent stops an event happening: prevent a fire. Protect keeps someone or something safe from harm: protect the building from fire. The grammar differs too: prevent something, but protect someone from something.

entry_json.avoid: Use prevent someone from doing something, not prevent someone to do something.

entry_json.definition: the amount of money you have to pay to buy something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The price of a monthly travel pass went up again this year.
example_sentences: House prices have risen faster than wages.
The price includes breakfast and parking.

confusables.difference: Price is the amount a seller asks for one item: the price of a ticket. Cost is the total money needed for something larger: the cost of living, the cost of building a hospital.
A price is what you pay. A prize is what you win. They look similar but the s in prize is said like a z.

entry_json.definition: to produce words or pictures on paper using a machine
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I print my notes because I find paper easier to revise from.
example_sentences: Please print your name in capital letters.
The library charges five pence per printed page.

entry_json.definition: a machine that prints words or pictures from a computer onto paper
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The printer in the study room jammed just before my deadline.
example_sentences: There is a printer on every floor of the library.
Our printer has run out of ink again.
collocations: the printer is out of paper

entry_json.definition: a building where people who break the law are kept locked in for a time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Some people argue that education reduces the number of people returning to prison.
example_sentences: He spent two years in prison for fraud.
The country has one of the largest prison populations in Europe.
entry_json.avoid: Say in prison with no article when you mean serving a sentence. In the prison means inside that particular building.

entry_json.definition: something you are given for winning a competition or doing very well
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She won first prize in the college writing competition.
example_sentences: The prize includes a place on a summer course.
Winning a prize looks good on an application.

confusables.difference: A prize is what you win, and it is said with a z sound. A price is what you pay, said with an s sound.
A prize comes from winning a competition. A reward is given for good behaviour, hard work or returning something lost.

entry_json.definition: used to say that something is likely to be true or to happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I will probably apply for the course again next year.
example_sentences: The meeting will probably last an hour.
She is probably the most experienced person on the team.
entry_json.avoid: Probably goes before the main verb but after will, is or are: he will probably come, she is probably right.

entry_json.definition: something difficult that causes trouble and that you must find an answer to
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The main problem with living far from the centre is the cost of travel.
example_sentences: Traffic is a serious problem in most large cities.
We solved the problem by changing the timetable.

confusables.difference: Problem clearly means something bad. Issue is a softer word for a subject that needs attention, and it may not be negative: an environmental issue.

entry_json.definition: a series of actions or changes that lead to a result
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Applying for a visa is a long process that takes several months.
example_sentences: The diagram shows the process of making paper.
Learning a language is a slow process.
entry_json.avoid: Task 1 process questions ask you to describe the stages in order, using words such as first, then, next and finally.

entry_json.definition: to make or grow something, especially in large amounts
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The region produces most of the country's fruit.
example_sentences: Factories in the area produce parts for cars.
Cows produce a large amount of methane.
entry_json.avoid: The verb produce is stressed on the second part. The noun produce, meaning fruit and vegetables, is stressed on the first.

entry_json.definition: something that is made or grown to be sold
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The company sells its products in more than thirty countries.
example_sentences: Dairy products are a large part of the region's exports.
Customers can return a product within thirty days.

entry_json.definition: connected with a job that needs special training, or done very well
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Getting professional advice before signing the contract saved me money.
example_sentences: She left teaching for a professional career in publishing.
The report was written in a professional tone.

confusables.difference: Professional means done as a paid job and to a high standard. Amateur means done for enjoyment without payment.

entry_json.definition: a university teacher at the highest level
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The professor who taught the module had written the main textbook.
example_sentences: She was made a professor at the age of forty.
Professor Ahmed will chair the discussion.

confusables.difference: In Britain, professor is the top academic rank at a university and is not used for school staff. School staff are teachers; other university staff are lecturers or tutors.

entry_json.avoid: Do not call your school or language teacher professor in British English.

entry_json.definition: a short description of a person, or the page about you on a website
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I updated my profile before applying for the internship.
example_sentences: Employers often look at a candidate's online profile.
The magazine ran a profile of the new director.

entry_json.definition: a set of instructions that tells a computer what to do
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I use a free program to check the grammar in my essays.
example_sentences: The program crashed and I lost ten minutes of work.
She writes programs for a small software company.

confusables.difference: In British English, program is only for computers and programme is everything else: a television programme, a training programme. American English uses program for all of them.

entry_json.definition: a show on television or radio, or a plan of activities
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a good documentary programme about cities on Thursday evenings.
example_sentences: The college runs a training programme for new staff.
She presents a weekly radio programme.

confusables.difference: Use programme for broadcasts and plans in British English, and program only for computer software. Do not mix the two spellings in one answer.

entry_json.definition: the process of getting better at something or moving towards a goal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I made real progress once I started speaking English every day.
example_sentences: The project has made little progress since March.
Regular tests show how much progress students are making.
entry_json.avoid: Progress is uncountable: say a lot of progress or some progress, never a progress or progresses.

entry_json.definition: a piece of work that you plan and then do over some time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Our final project was to design a transport plan for a small town.
example_sentences: The building project will take three years to finish.
Students work in groups on a research project.
entry_json.avoid: The noun project is stressed on the first part; the verb to project is stressed on the second.

entry_json.definition: to say that you will certainly do something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I promised my parents that I would call every Sunday.
example_sentences: The government promised to build more affordable homes.
She promised to send the notes before the exam.

entry_json.definition: to make the sound of a word or letter
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I still find it hard to pronounce the th sound at the start of a word.
example_sentences: How do you pronounce your surname?
The letter h is not pronounced in that word.
entry_json.avoid: The noun is pronunciation, with no ou in the middle. Do not write pronounciation.

entry_json.definition: to keep someone or something safe from things that could hurt it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Planting trees along the river protects the banks from flooding.
example_sentences: Sun cream protects your skin from damage.
The law protects workers from unfair dismissal.

confusables.difference: Protect keeps something safe: protect the forest. Prevent stops an event: prevent the fire. Protect takes someone from something; prevent takes something or someone from doing something.

entry_json.definition: to give someone something that they need
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The college provides free language support for international students.
example_sentences: The charity provides meals for people with no home.
Solar panels provide most of the building's electricity.
entry_json.avoid: Say provide something for someone or provide someone with something. Do not say provide someone something.

entry_json.definition: a building in Britain where people go to drink and often to eat
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We usually meet in a quiet pub near the station after work.
example_sentences: The village pub is the only place people can meet in the evening.
Many local pubs have closed in the last ten years.
entry_json.avoid: Pub is short for public house. It is a normal everyday word in Britain, but it is informal, so use it in speaking rather than Task 2.

entry_json.definition: for everyone to use, or connected with all the people in a country
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Public transport in my city is cheap but very crowded at peak times.
example_sentences: Public libraries are free to join.
There is growing public concern about air quality.

confusables.difference: Public means open to everyone or run by the state: a public hospital. Private means owned by a person or company and often paid for: a private clinic.

entry_json.definition: to print a book, magazine or article and make it available to people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The results of the study were published in a medical journal.
example_sentences: She published her first novel at the age of thirty.
The council publishes the figures every quarter.

entry_json.definition: to move something towards you using your hands
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Pull the handle firmly because the door sticks in wet weather.
example_sentences: He pulled the chair closer to the desk.
The sign on the door says pull, not push.

confusables.difference: They are opposites. Pull brings something towards you; push moves it away from you.

entry_json.definition: having the colour you get when you put red and blue together
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She wore a dark purple jacket to the interview.
example_sentences: The hills look purple in the evening light.
The chart uses purple for the second group.

entry_json.definition: the reason for which something is done or made
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The purpose of the survey was to find out how students travel to college.
example_sentences: The building was designed for a very different purpose.
She went to the meeting with a clear purpose.

confusables.difference: A purpose is the aim you want to achieve, looking forward. A reason explains why something happened, often looking back.

entry_json.avoid: On purpose means deliberately, which is a different meaning from the purpose of something.

entry_json.definition: to move something away from you using your hands
entry_json.own_context_sentence: You have to push the door hard because it is heavy.
example_sentences: She pushed her bike up the hill.
Do not push in front of people who are waiting.

confusables.difference: Push moves something away from you; pull brings it towards you. British shop doors are usually marked with one of these two words.

entry_json.definition: to move something into a particular place or position
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I put my phone in another room when I need to concentrate.
example_sentences: Put your bag under the seat in front of you.
She put the results into a simple table.
entry_json.avoid: Put does not change in the past: I put it there yesterday, not I putted.

entry_json.definition: how good or bad something is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The quality of the teaching mattered more to me than the price.
example_sentences: Air quality in the city has improved since the low emission zone opened.
These shoes are expensive but the quality is excellent.

confusables.difference: Quality is how good something is; quantity is how much of it there is. A small quantity of high quality food is a normal thing to say.

entry_json.definition: an amount or a number of something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Large quantities of food are thrown away by supermarkets every day.
example_sentences: The recipe uses only a small quantity of oil.
We measured the quantity of water each household used.

confusables.difference: Quantity answers how much or how many; quality answers how good. Do not use one when you mean the other.

entry_json.definition: one of four parts of something, all the same size
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Almost a quarter of the students in my class work part time.
example_sentences: Cut the apple into quarters.
The train leaves at a quarter past six.
entry_json.avoid: For time, say a quarter past six and a quarter to seven in British English.

entry_json.definition: a woman who rules a country, or the wife of a king
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The queen opened the new hospital wing last year.
example_sentences: Britain has had several queens who ruled in their own right.
The palace was built for a queen in the sixteenth century.

entry_json.definition: a sentence or phrase that asks for information
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Read the question twice before you start writing your answer.
example_sentences: The examiner will ask you three questions about your home town.
Nobody could answer the last question in the test.
entry_json.avoid: Say ask a question, not do a question or make a question.

entry_json.definition: taking only a short time, or moving fast
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I had a quick look at the notes before the lesson started.
example_sentences: There is no quick solution to traffic in a growing city.
She gave a quick answer without thinking.

confusables.difference: Fast is usually about speed of movement: a fast train. Quick is usually about a short time: a quick meeting. A fast car is not the same as a quick car.

entry_json.definition: in a short time or at a fast speed
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city has grown quickly over the last twenty years.
example_sentences: Read the questions quickly before you listen.
News travels quickly on social media.

entry_json.definition: making very little noise
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I look for a quiet corner of the library when I want to concentrate.
example_sentences: The street is quiet at night because there is no through traffic.
Please keep the room quiet during the test.

confusables.difference: Quiet has two syllables and means with little noise. Quite has one syllable and means fairly or completely. A quiet room is silent, a quite good room is only fairly good.

entry_json.definition: in a way that makes very little noise
entry_json.own_context_sentence: He closed the door quietly so that he would not wake anyone.
example_sentences: She spoke so quietly that I could not hear the answer.
Please work quietly while the exam is in progress.

entry_json.definition: a little, but not very; with some words it can mean completely
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course was quite demanding, but the support was good.
example_sentences: It is quite cold this morning.
I am not quite ready to leave.

confusables.difference: Quite means fairly and has one syllable. Quiet means with little noise and has two. This is one of the most common spelling slips in IELTS writing.

entry_json.avoid: With strong adjectives, quite means completely: quite impossible means totally impossible, not fairly impossible.

entry_json.definition: a device that receives sounds sent through the air, or the programmes it plays
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I listen to the radio in the car because it keeps me up to date.
example_sentences: Local radio still reaches many older listeners.
She was interviewed on national radio.

entry_json.definition: the metal tracks that trains travel on, and the whole train system
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The railway between the two cities was built in the nineteenth century.
example_sentences: A new railway line will cut the journey by half an hour.
The railway station is a short walk from my flat.

confusables.difference: Railway is British English and railroad is American English. IELTS listening uses the British form.

entry_json.definition: water that falls from the clouds in drops
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Heavy rain in October caused flooding across the whole region.
example_sentences: The rain stopped just before the match started.
Farmers here depend on the rain arriving in June.
entry_json.avoid: Rain is normally uncountable: heavy rain, not a heavy rain.

entry_json.definition: to lift something up, or to increase an amount
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The college raised its fees by five per cent this year.
example_sentences: Please raise your hand if you have a question.
The charity raised twenty thousand pounds for new equipment.

confusables.difference: Raise needs an object: someone raises something. Rise does not: something rises by itself. Prices rise, but the company raises prices.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write prices raised last year. Write prices rose or the government raised prices.

entry_json.definition: how often something happens, or the speed or price of something compared with something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The unemployment rate fell steadily between 2015 and 2019.
example_sentences: The birth rate has dropped in most developed countries.
Interest rates were raised again last month.

entry_json.definition: quite, or a little, often about something that is not very good
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The lecture was rather long, but the last part was useful.
example_sentences: The instructions were rather confusing.
I would rather walk than wait for the bus.
entry_json.avoid: Would rather is followed by a bare verb: I would rather stay, not I would rather to stay.

entry_json.definition: to arrive at a place, or to put your hand out to touch something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We reached the hotel just before midnight.
example_sentences: Temperatures reached forty degrees last summer.
She reached for her phone to check the time.

confusables.difference: Reach takes a direct object with no preposition: reach the station. Arrive needs one: arrive at the station, arrive in London.

entry_json.avoid: Do not say reach to the station. Reach takes the place directly.

entry_json.definition: to behave in a particular way because of something that has happened
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Most people reacted calmly when the fire alarm went off.
example_sentences: The government reacted quickly to the flooding.
How did your family react to the news?
entry_json.avoid: Use react to something, not react on something.

entry_json.definition: to look at words on a page or a screen and understand them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I read for half an hour every night before I sleep.
example_sentences: She read the whole report before the meeting.
Read the instructions carefully before you begin.
entry_json.avoid: The past form is spelt read but said like red. Only the sound changes.

entry_json.definition: a person who reads, especially someone who reads a particular newspaper or book
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Newspapers have lost readers to free news websites.
example_sentences: The magazine has half a million readers.
She is a fast reader and finishes a novel in two days.

entry_json.definition: the activity of looking at words on a page or a screen and understanding them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Reading in English every day improved my vocabulary faster than anything else.
example_sentences: The reading section of the test lasts one hour.
Wide reading helps with both writing and speaking.

entry_json.definition: having everything you need, so you can do something now
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I did not feel ready for the exam until the last week.
example_sentences: Dinner will be ready in ten minutes.
Are you ready to start?
entry_json.avoid: Use ready for a noun and ready to before a verb: ready for the test, ready to leave.

entry_json.definition: actually existing and not imagined or false
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a real risk that the river will flood again this winter.
example_sentences: The film is based on a real event.
That is the real reason she left the job.

confusables.difference: Real is an adjective and goes with a noun: a real problem. Really is an adverb and goes with a verb or adjective: really difficult. Do not say it was real difficult.

entry_json.definition: to understand or start to know something that you did not know before
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I only realized how much I relied on my phone when I lost it.
example_sentences: She realized that she had left her keys inside.
Many people do not realize how much water a shower uses.

confusables.difference: Realize means to understand a fact for the first time. Recognize means to know someone or something because you have seen it before.

entry_json.definition: very, or actually and in fact
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course was really useful, especially the speaking sessions.
example_sentences: I do not really know the answer.
Is that really what she said?
entry_json.avoid: Really is common in speech but weak in Task 2 writing. Use very, extremely, particularly or genuinely instead.

entry_json.definition: the cause of something, or why someone does something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The main reason I moved was to be closer to my family.
example_sentences: There are several reasons for the fall in numbers.
She gave no reason for cancelling the meeting.
entry_json.avoid: Say the reason for something or the reason why he left, but never the reason why is because.

entry_json.definition: to get something that someone sends or gives you
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I received the offer letter two weeks after the interview.
example_sentences: Students receive their results by email.
The charity received a large donation last year.

confusables.difference: Receive just means something arrived; accept means you agreed to take it. You can receive an invitation and still not accept it.

entry_json.avoid: Spelling: i before e except after c. Write receive, not recieve.

entry_json.definition: having happened or been made a short time ago
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A recent study found that students who sleep well score higher.
example_sentences: In recent years, the city has built several cycle lanes.
The most recent figures come from last March.

entry_json.definition: a short time ago
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I recently started cycling to work instead of driving.
example_sentences: Until recently, the building was a factory.
She has recently finished her training.
entry_json.avoid: Recently is often used with the present perfect: she has recently moved. With the past simple it usually refers to a definite moment.

entry_json.definition: the area near the door of a hotel or office where visitors are met and helped
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Please leave your name at reception before going up to the office.
example_sentences: Reception is open from eight until six.
The signal is poor, so mobile reception is weak inside the building.

entry_json.definition: a set of instructions telling you how to cook something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I follow a simple recipe for lentil soup that takes twenty minutes.
example_sentences: The recipe uses only five ingredients.
She learned the recipe from her grandmother.

confusables.difference: A recipe tells you how to cook. A receipt is the paper that proves you paid. Receipt is said with a silent p.

entry_json.definition: to know someone or something because you have seen or heard them before
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I did not recognize my old school because it had been rebuilt.
example_sentences: The software recognizes your voice after a few minutes.
She recognized his name on the list immediately.

confusables.difference: Recognize is about knowing something again from before. Realize is about understanding a fact for the first time.
Both spellings are accepted in British English. Keep the same one throughout your answer.

entry_json.definition: to tell someone that something is good and that they should try it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I would recommend arriving thirty minutes before the test starts.
example_sentences: My tutor recommended a book that explained the topic clearly.
Doctors recommend at least seven hours of sleep.
entry_json.avoid: Say recommend doing something or recommend that someone do something. Do not say recommend me to do it.

entry_json.definition: information that people write down and keep so that it can be looked at later, or the best result so far
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The hospital keeps a record of every appointment.
example_sentences: Last July broke the record for the hottest month.
Schools must keep records of attendance.
entry_json.avoid: The noun record is stressed on the first part; the verb to record is stressed on the second.

entry_json.definition: sound or pictures that have been stored so they can be played again
entry_json.own_context_sentence: You will hear the recording only once in the listening test.
example_sentences: She listened to the recording of the lecture twice.
The recording was too quiet to understand.

entry_json.definition: to make old things such as paper or glass into new things so that they can be used again
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Our building recycles glass and paper but not food waste.
example_sentences: Only a small share of plastic is actually recycled.
Aluminium can be recycled many times without losing quality.

confusables.difference: Reuse means using the same object again as it is. Recycle means breaking it down to make something new.

entry_json.definition: having the colour of blood
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The chart uses a red line to show the increase in energy use.
example_sentences: She was wearing a red coat.
The traffic light turned red just as we arrived.

entry_json.definition: to make something smaller in size, amount or number
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Working from home reduced my travel costs by half.
example_sentences: The council wants to reduce traffic in the city centre.
Cycling reduces the risk of heart disease.

confusables.difference: Reduce usually needs someone to do it: the company reduced prices. Decrease often happens by itself: sales decreased. In Task 1, figures decrease, but a policy reduces them.

entry_json.definition: to mention or talk about someone or something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The writer refers to three earlier studies in the opening paragraph.
example_sentences: The figures refer to the year ending in March.
Please refer to page ten for the full table.
entry_json.avoid: Refer needs to before its object: refer to the report. The double r appears in referred and referring.

entry_json.definition: a large area of a country or of the world
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The northern region of the country receives far more rain than the south.
example_sentences: Unemployment is higher in some regions than others.
The region is known for its wine.

confusables.difference: Area is the general word and can be any size. Region is larger and usually means a recognized part of a country with its own character.

entry_json.definition: happening again and again with the same amount of time in between
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Regular exercise made a bigger difference to my sleep than anything else.
example_sentences: The bus service is regular during the week but poor at weekends.
She is a regular visitor to the library.

entry_json.definition: the way two people or things are connected to each other
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a clear relationship between income and life expectancy.
example_sentences: She has a good relationship with her colleagues.
The study looked at the relationship between diet and sleep.
entry_json.avoid: Use the relationship between two things or with a person: a relationship with my manager.

entry_json.definition: to rest and stop feeling worried or busy
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I relax by cooking, because it takes my mind off work.
example_sentences: Try to relax before the speaking test.
At the weekend I relax with a book in the park.

confusables.difference: Relaxed describes how you feel: I feel relaxed. Relaxing describes what causes the feeling: a relaxing evening. The same pattern applies to bored and boring.

entry_json.definition: to keep something in your mind, or to bring it back into your mind
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I still remember my first day at secondary school clearly.
example_sentences: Remember to bring your passport to the test.
I cannot remember where I put the tickets.

confusables.difference: You remember something yourself. Someone else reminds you: please remind me to call her. Do not say remember me to call her.

entry_json.avoid: Remember to do means do not forget in the future. Remember doing means you have a memory of the past.

entry_json.definition: to take something away from a place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The council removed the old bus shelter and put nothing in its place.
example_sentences: Please remove your shoes before entering.
The filter removes most of the dust from the air.

entry_json.definition: to fix something that is broken or not working
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It cost less to repair my laptop than to buy a new one.
example_sentences: The road is being repaired, so expect delays.
He repaired the bike himself using online videos.

confusables.difference: They mean the same, but fix is more informal and common in speech. Repair sounds more formal and suits written English.

entry_json.definition: to say or do something again
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Could you repeat the question, please?
example_sentences: The teacher repeated the instructions slowly.
She had to repeat the year after failing two subjects.
entry_json.avoid: Do not say repeat again, as repeat already means again.

entry_json.definition: to put a new thing in the place of an old one
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The old windows were replaced with double glazing to cut heating bills.
example_sentences: Machines have replaced many workers on the production line.
I need to replace my phone battery.
entry_json.avoid: Use replace A with B: they replaced the old system with a new one. Do not say replace by in this pattern in everyday writing.

entry_json.definition: to answer someone by speaking or writing
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The company replied to my application within a week.
example_sentences: She replied that she was not available on Friday.
Please reply to this email by Friday.

confusables.difference: Answer takes a direct object: answer the question. Reply needs to: reply to the question. Reply also fits letters and emails better.

entry_json.definition: a piece of writing or a talk that tells people about something that has happened
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The report shows that air quality improved after the new zone opened.
example_sentences: The committee published its report in June.
According to the report, numbers fell by ten per cent.

entry_json.definition: a person whose job is to collect news and write or speak about it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A reporter interviewed local residents about the new road.
example_sentences: The reporter spent a month investigating the story.
She started her career as a local reporter.

entry_json.definition: the act of politely asking for something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sent a request for an extension and my tutor agreed the same day.
example_sentences: The library will consider requests for new books.
Copies of the report are available on request.

entry_json.definition: careful study of a subject in order to find out new facts
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Recent research suggests that short walks improve concentration.
example_sentences: She is doing research into air quality in schools.
The university is well known for its medical research.
entry_json.avoid: Research is uncountable: much research or a piece of research, never a research or researches.

entry_json.definition: a person whose job is to study a subject and find out new facts
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Researchers followed two thousand people over ten years.
example_sentences: The researchers interviewed families in three cities.
She works as a researcher at a medical institute.

entry_json.definition: to say or do something because of what someone else has said or done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The council responded to complaints by adding more bins.
example_sentences: Only half the people responded to the survey.
Patients responded well to the new treatment.

confusables.difference: Answer is the everyday word and takes a direct object: answer the phone. Respond is more formal and takes to: respond to an email.

entry_json.definition: what someone says or does because of something that has happened
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The response to the new timetable was mostly positive.
example_sentences: I have had no response to my application yet.
In response to the flooding, the council built a new wall.

entry_json.definition: a place where you buy and eat a meal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We only eat in a restaurant on special occasions because it is expensive.
example_sentences: The restaurant near the station serves food until eleven.
Many small restaurants closed during the last few years.

entry_json.definition: something that happens because of something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: As a result of the new bus lane, journey times fell by ten minutes.
example_sentences: The exam results come out in six weeks.
The study produced surprising results.
entry_json.avoid: As a result stands alone, but as a result of is followed by a noun: as a result of the strike.

entry_json.definition: to come or go back to a place, or to give something back
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I returned the books to the library a day late and had to pay a fine.
example_sentences: She returned home after four years abroad.
Many students do not return to their home town after graduating.
entry_json.avoid: Return already means go back. Do not write return back.

entry_json.definition: a report that gives an opinion about a book, film or product; also a careful look at something again
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I read several reviews before choosing the course.
example_sentences: The film received good reviews from critics.
The council is carrying out a review of parking charges.

entry_json.definition: a food of small hard white or brown pieces from a plant, that you cook in water and eat
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rice is the main food in my country and we eat it twice a day.
example_sentences: Growing rice uses a very large amount of water.
Boil the rice for about twelve minutes.
entry_json.avoid: Rice is uncountable: some rice or a bowl of rice, never a rice.

entry_json.definition: having a lot of money
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The gap between rich and poor has widened in the last twenty years.
example_sentences: Only rich countries can afford this kind of programme.
The region is rich in natural resources.
entry_json.avoid: The rich means rich people in general and takes a plural verb: the rich pay more tax.

entry_json.definition: to sit on a bicycle, motorcycle or horse and control it as it moves
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I ride my bike to work whenever the weather allows.
example_sentences: She learned to ride a horse as a child.
Riding a bicycle in heavy traffic can feel dangerous.
entry_json.avoid: You ride a bike or a horse, but you drive a car and you go by bus.

entry_json.definition: correct, or on the side of your body that most people write with
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I am not sure this is the right answer, but it is my best guess.
example_sentences: Turn right at the end of the road.
She made the right decision in changing courses.

confusables.difference: Right means correct or the opposite of left. Write means to put words on paper. They sound the same, so check the spelling.

entry_json.definition: to go up or to increase
entry_json.own_context_sentence: House prices rose sharply between 2010 and 2020.
example_sentences: Temperatures rise steadily through the morning.
The number of students rose by five per cent.

confusables.difference: Rise happens on its own and takes no object: prices rise. Raise needs an object: the shop raises prices. The past forms are rose and risen for rise, but raised for raise.

entry_json.avoid: Do not write the government rose taxes. Write raised taxes, or taxes rose.

entry_json.definition: a long line of water that moves across the land towards the sea
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The river runs straight through the centre of the city.
example_sentences: Factories once poured waste directly into the river.
We walked along the river as far as the old bridge.

entry_json.definition: a long hard way built for cars and buses to travel on between places
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The road into the city is busiest between seven and nine.
example_sentences: A new road has cut the journey by twenty minutes.
Heavy rain closed the main road to the north.

confusables.difference: A street is a road in a town with buildings along both sides. A road can be anywhere, including between towns.

entry_json.definition: the job or part that someone or something has in a situation
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Parents play an important role in how children view education.
example_sentences: Technology plays a growing role in modern teaching.
She took on a new role in the marketing team.

confusables.difference: A role is the part you play; a rule is something you must obey. They sound different, but learners often mix the spellings: play a role, follow a rule.

entry_json.definition: the part that covers the top of a building
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Solar panels on the roof cover most of our electricity in summer.
example_sentences: The storm damaged the roof of the old school.
There is a small garden on the roof of the building.

entry_json.definition: a part of a building with its own walls and door; also space for something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My room is small, but it has a large window and plenty of light.
example_sentences: The flat has three rooms and a shared kitchen.
There is not enough room in the bag for another book.
entry_json.avoid: When room means space it is uncountable: is there room for one more, not a room for one more.

entry_json.definition: shaped like a circle or a ball
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The table in the meeting room is round, so everyone can see each other.
example_sentences: The chart is a round diagram divided into five parts.
She wore round glasses.

entry_json.definition: the way you travel from one place to another
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I take a longer route to work because it avoids the main road.
example_sentences: The bus route was changed to serve the new hospital.
This is the quickest route to the airport.
entry_json.avoid: In British English route is said like root. The American pronunciation can sound like rout.

entry_json.definition: the usual way you do things, in the same order, again and again
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My daily routine changed completely when I started studying in the evenings.
example_sentences: Children benefit from a regular bedtime routine.
Working from home broke my old morning routine.

entry_json.definition: things that you throw away because you do not want them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The council collects rubbish once a week and recycling once a fortnight.
example_sentences: There was rubbish all over the park after the festival.
Households are asked to sort their rubbish before collection.

confusables.difference: Rubbish is British English; garbage and trash are American. IELTS listening uses rubbish, so learn it for the British test.

entry_json.avoid: Rubbish is uncountable: a lot of rubbish, never a rubbish or rubbishes.

entry_json.definition: not polite, and likely to make other people angry or unhappy
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It is considered rude here to arrive very late without telling anyone.
example_sentences: He was rude to the staff and was asked to leave.
In some cultures it is rude to refuse food.

confusables.difference: They are opposites. Rude ignores other people's feelings; polite respects them. Direct commands can sound rude in English, so use could or would.

entry_json.definition: something that tells you what you must or must not do
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The rule about mobile phones in the exam room is very strict.
example_sentences: Every player must follow the rules of the game.
The school changed its rules on uniform last year.

confusables.difference: A rule applies inside a group or place, such as a school or a game. A law applies to everyone in a country and is enforced by the courts.

entry_json.definition: to move quickly using your legs; also to be the person who controls a business or activity
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I run in the park three times a week before breakfast.
example_sentences: She runs a small business from home.
The buses run every fifteen minutes.
entry_json.avoid: The past forms are ran and have run: I ran yesterday, I have run twice this week.

entry_json.definition: a person who runs, especially in a race or for exercise
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The park is full of runners early on Saturday mornings.
example_sentences: Over forty thousand runners took part in the marathon.
She is a serious runner and trains six days a week.

entry_json.definition: the activity or sport of moving quickly on your legs
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Running is the cheapest exercise I know, because it needs no equipment.
example_sentences: Running has become very popular among office workers.
She took up running after an injury stopped her playing football.

entry_json.definition: unhappy, or making you feel unhappy
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I felt sad leaving my home town, even though the move was my choice.
example_sentences: It is sad that so many local shops have closed.
She looked sad when she heard the news.

entry_json.definition: in an unhappy way, or used to say that you are sorry something is true
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Sadly, the swimming pool closed before the new one was finished.
example_sentences: Sadly, very few students took up the offer.
She smiled sadly and said nothing.

confusables.difference: They both introduce bad news. Unfortunately is more neutral and slightly more formal, so it fits Task 2 better. Sadly adds real emotion.

entry_json.definition: not in danger, and not likely to hurt anyone
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The streets here feel safe even late at night.
example_sentences: Cycle lanes make the roads safer for everyone.
Is the water safe to drink?

confusables.difference: Safe is an adjective and ends with an f sound. Save is a verb, ends with a v sound, and means to keep or rescue. Do not write drive safe when you mean drive safely.

entry_json.definition: to travel across water in a boat or ship
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We sailed across the bay in less than an hour.
example_sentences: The ferry sails twice a day in winter.
They sailed from Southampton to New York.

confusables.difference: Sail means to travel by boat. A sale is the act of selling, or a period of lower prices. They sound the same, so check the spelling.

entry_json.definition: the sport or activity of travelling in a boat with sails
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Sailing is popular here because the town is right on the coast.
example_sentences: He took up sailing after moving to the coast.
The club offers sailing lessons for beginners.

entry_json.definition: a cold dish of vegetables that are not cooked, often eaten with a meal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I make a large salad on Sunday and eat it during the week.
example_sentences: The cafe serves a salad with every sandwich.
A green salad is the cheapest thing on the menu.
